name: walkthrough
title: Parser Combinators: Parsers as First-Class Values
description: Walk through building a parser combinator library from atomic parsers to a complete Mini expression parser with AST construction.

steps.description: Set up with try-except wrapper
Define char parser that matches one exact character
Test char parser on string abc at position 0

steps.question: What does char('a') return on 'abc' at position 0?

steps.description: Move to atomic parsers
Import re for regex support
Re-define char parser
Define satisfy parser for character classes
Define regex parser for pattern matching

steps.question: What does lit('if') return on 'if x' at position 0?

steps.description: Move to combinator primitives
Re-define atomic parsers inline
Define seq combinator for sequencing parsers
Define alt combinator for alternation
Define many and many1 for repetition
Define pmap for transforming parser results

steps.question: What does word parse from 'hello world'?

steps.description: Move to recursive parsers with forward references
Import re and define minimal combinator library
Define Forward class for forward references
Create forward references for expr, term, factor
Define number, parentheses, and operator parsers with tokens
Define factor parser with parenthesized expressions
Define term parser with multiplication and division
Define expr parser with addition and subtraction
Move to parsers as a monad
Define Parser class with __call__ method
Define pure classmethod for return monad operation
Define bind method for monadic sequencing
Define map method in terms of bind
Build sum parser using bind, then, and map
Move to complete Mini expression parser with AST
Define minimal Parser monad and combinators
Define tok helper for token parsing with whitespace
Define AST node classes: Num, BinOp, UnaryMinus
Define FwdP class for forward parser references
Define token parsers and set up forward references
Define primary parser with numbers and parentheses
Define unary parser for negative numbers
Define left_assoc helper and term/expr parsers

steps.question: What tree does '2 + 3 * 4' produce?
steps.answer: '2 + 3 * 4'           tree: BinOp('+', Num(2.0), BinOp('*', Num(3.0), Num(4.0)))  value: 14.0

Set up for committed choice simulation

steps.answer: committed_alt defined (see Parsec's 'try' for the full story)
